messages:
Sam: Hi @people-ops — baby arrived 35 days ago! Trying to add newborn to medical + dental. Missed the 30-day window because hospital delayed the birth certificate. Can we still add them and get coverage backdated to birth? I also don't have the SSN yet. :baby:
Leah (People Ops): Congrats, Sam! :tada: Birth is a qualifying life event. Our standard window is 30 days, but we do exception reviews for documentation delays.
Sam: What docs will you need? I have the hospital discharge summary and a temporary birth record but the official certificate is stuck with the county (processing backlog).
Ravi (Benefits): Short answer: collect as much proof as you can. Carriers often accept hospital discharge, attending physician statement, temporary birth record, and then the official certificate when it arrives.
Leah (People Ops): Action list for you: 1) Upload hospital discharge summary (PDF). 2) Upload temporary birth record / hospital-issued birth verification. 3) If you have any receipt/confirmation from the county stating processing delay, include that. 4) Fill out the "Change Outside Open Enrollment" form in the benefits portal and choose "New dependent - documentation delay". 5) Email the portal confirmation to benefits@redwood.com with subject: "BEN-EXCEPTION-1793456789".
Sam: If exception is approved, will coverage be effective from the birth date? I already had a pediatric appt and one ER visit that generated a bill.
Ravi (Benefits): Carrier policies differ. If they approve the exception and accept the docs, they can make the effective date the birth date and potentialy reimburse eligible claims. We'll ask for itemized bills and claim forms to submit retro claims. Not guaranteed, but we escalate for newborns with immediate care.
Sam: About SSN — SSA says it can take weeks. Do I need to wait for SSN to enroll?
Leah (People Ops): No, don't wait. On the portal enter "SSN pending" and upload the SSA application receipt when you have it. Add passport or state ID for the parent(s). The carrier may request SSN later once issued.
Sam: Any filename convention for uploads?
Leah (People Ops): Please name files like: "Lastname_BabyFirstname_docTYPE_DATE.pdf" (e.g., Kim_Aria_birthverify_2026-03-06.pdf). It speeds processing.
BenefitsBot: Submission received: Ticket BEN-1793456789 created. An intake rep will route to Benefits for review.
Leah (People Ops): Turnaround: we submit to the carrier same day we have the packet. Carrier response usually 5-10 business days; we'll post updates here.
Sam: Great, uploading discharge summary and temporary birth record now. Also attaching the ER itemized bill per Ravi.
Ravi (Benefits): Thanks — once the packet is in I'll flag the claims team so they can prep claim forms. If the carrier approves retro coverage, claim reimbursement is possible if claims meet plan rules.
Leah (People Ops): Quick note: if carrier asks for a signed physician statement, we'll request it from you and provide a template.
Sam: Appreciate it, everyone — really helps.
Leah (People Ops): Happy to help. I'll follow up when carrier responds. :pray:
